A parallel Fortran framework for neural networks and deep learning
. It reshapes each digit into a one-channel

children.html: 28×2828 \times 2828×28

children.value: image, applies two convolutions and two max-pools, and finishes with a 10-way softmax. The library inserts a flatten layer where a dense layer follows a rank-3 map.

program cnn_mnist

  use nf, only: network, sgd, &
    input, conv, maxpool, flatten, dense, reshape, &
    load_mnist, label_digits, softmax, relu

  implicit none

  type(network) :: net

  real, allocatable :: training_images(:,:), training_labels(:)
  real, allocatable :: validation_images(:,:), validation_labels(:)
  real, allocatable :: testing_images(:,:), testing_labels(:)
  integer :: n
  integer, parameter :: num_epochs = 20

  call load_mnist(training_images, training_labels, &
                  validation_images, validation_labels, &
                  testing_images, testing_labels)

  net = network([ &
    input(784), &
    reshape(1, 28, 28), &
    conv(filters=8, kernel_width=3, kernel_height=3, activation=relu()), &
    maxpool(pool_width=2, pool_height=2, stride=2), &
    conv(filters=16, kernel_width=3, kernel_height=3, activation=relu()), &
    maxpool(pool_width=2, pool_height=2, stride=2), &
    dense(10, activation=softmax()) &
  ])

  call net % print_info()
is called with the optional test arrays, so this program loads the 10000 test images as well as the 50000 training and 10000 validation images.

The epoch loop and the accuracy

children.label: The epoch loop and the accuracy

children.value:
epochs: do n = 1, num_epochs

    call net % train( &
      training_images, &
      label_digits(training_labels), &
      batch_size=16, &
      epochs=1, &
      optimizer=sgd(learning_rate=0.001) &
    )

    print '(a,i2,a,f5.2,a)', 'Epoch ', n, ' done, Accuracy: ', accuracy( &
      net, validation_images, label_digits(validation_labels)) * 100, ' %'

  end do epochs

  print '(a,f5.2,a)', 'Testing accuracy: ', &
    accuracy(net, testing_images, label_digits(testing_labels)) * 100, '%'

contains

  real function accuracy(net, x, y)
    type(network), intent(in out) :: net
    real, intent(in) :: x(:,:), y(:,:)
    integer :: i, good
    good = 0
    do i = 1, size(x, dim=2)
      if (all(maxloc(net % predict(x(:,i))) == maxloc(y(:,i)))) then
        good = good + 1
      end if
    end do
    accuracy = real(good) / size(x, dim=2)
  end function accuracy
The loop runs 20 epochs. Each call to
uses one epoch, batch size 16, and SGD with learning rate 0.001. As in the dense program, a step is a random contiguous window, and
divides the gradient by the batch size. There are

program cnn_mnist

  use nf, only: network, sgd, &
    input, conv, maxpool, flatten, dense, reshape, &
    load_mnist, label_digits, softmax, relu

  implicit none

  type(network) :: net

  real, allocatable :: training_images(:,:), training_labels(:)
  real, allocatable :: validation_images(:,:), validation_labels(:)
  real, allocatable :: testing_images(:,:), testing_labels(:)
  integer :: n
  integer, parameter :: num_epochs = 20

  call load_mnist(training_images, training_labels, &
                  validation_images, validation_labels, &
                  testing_images, testing_labels)

  net = network([ &
    input(784), &
    reshape(1, 28, 28), &
    conv(filters=8, kernel_width=3, kernel_height=3, activation=relu()), &
    maxpool(pool_width=2, pool_height=2, stride=2), &
    conv(filters=16, kernel_width=3, kernel_height=3, activation=relu()), &
    maxpool(pool_width=2, pool_height=2, stride=2), &
    dense(10, activation=softmax()) &
  ])

  call net % print_info()

  epochs: do n = 1, num_epochs

    call net % train( &
      training_images, &
      label_digits(training_labels), &
      batch_size=16, &
      epochs=1, &
      optimizer=sgd(learning_rate=0.001) &
    )

    print '(a,i2,a,f5.2,a)', 'Epoch ', n, ' done, Accuracy: ', accuracy( &
      net, validation_images, label_digits(validation_labels)) * 100, ' %'

  end do epochs

  print '(a,f5.2,a)', 'Testing accuracy: ', &
    accuracy(net, testing_images, label_digits(testing_labels)) * 100, '%'

contains

  real function accuracy(net, x, y)
    type(network), intent(in out) :: net
    real, intent(in) :: x(:,:), y(:,:)
    integer :: i, good
    good = 0
    do i = 1, size(x, dim=2)
      if (all(maxloc(net % predict(x(:,i))) == maxloc(y(:,i)))) then
        good = good + 1
      end if
    end do
    accuracy = real(good) / size(x, dim=2)
  end function accuracy

end program cnn_mnist
The package file below builds this source with fpm. The Fortran program itself is the file from the repository.

name = "Section_Examples_Cnn_Mnist"

[build]
auto-executables = true
auto-tests = true
auto-examples = true

[install]
library = false

[dependencies]
neural-fortran = { git = "https://github.com/modern-fortran/neural-fortran.git" }

[[executable]]
name = "Section_Examples_Cnn_Mnist"
source-dir = "app"
main = "cnn_mnist.f90"

The convolution program uses the same

accuracy as the dense MNIST example. On this run the validation accuracy reaches 90.94 percent at epoch 16. Epoch 20 prints 9.83 percent, and the test accuracy measured after that epoch is 9.82 percent. The program does not keep the earlier weights. The saved run is the collapsed network, and the page reports that number.
